image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor). The image captures the anterior to mid-section of the fish, showing the characteristic black head and front body transitioning into a bright yellow posterior. The eye is visible on the far left edge. The background is a blurred blue-grey, suggesting an underwater environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small protrusible mouth with brush-like teeth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is located at the very tip of the snout, which is cut off by the left edge of the frame. It is not visible.
The eye is partially visible on the extreme left edge. While cropped, the visible portion shows a large, dark pupil consistent with the species' anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible curvature of the dorsal and ventral profiles indicates a deep, laterally compressed body typical of angelfish/butterflyfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic black anterior section and yellow posterior section. The transition is sharp and distinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is visible along the top edge. It appears continuous. While individual rays are hard to distinguish due to resolution, the structure is intact and follows the body contour correctly.
The anal fin is visible on the bottom edge, mirroring the dorsal fin's position and appearing structurally sound.
The tail (caudal fin) is completely outside the frame on the right side.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The black scales exhibit a slightly uniform, noisy texture that lacks the distinct individual scale definition seen in high-quality macro photography, suggesting mild AI smoothing or generation noise.

There is a noticeable lack of sharpness around the eye and the cut-off snout. The focus seems to drift rapidly, which could be depth-of-field but also resembles common AI generation softness at object boundaries.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification given the distinctive color pattern, ensuring it is not a generic angelfish or misclassified species.
To check for 'melting' artifacts where the fins meet the water background and to ensure the black/yellow color boundary is sharp and physically plausible.
To assess the naturalness of the skin/scale texture and identify any subtle generative noise or unnatural blurring patterns.

focus_areas: Scale texture realism in the black vs. yellow regions
Sharpness and integrity of the dorsal and anal fin edges
Color boundary precision between black and yellow sections
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the black scales; AI often smears this into a flat matte black rather than showing individual scales. Verify if the eye structure, though partially cropped, maintains correct anatomical roundness and reflection. Check if the fin edges bleed into the background.
